name: Lidocaine (systemic)
dosing: IV bolus for ventricular arrhythmias typically 1–1.5 mg/kg followed by infusion per local protocol (e.g., 1–4 mg/min titrated to response); dosing for local infiltration/topical use differs—follow product guidance
contraindications: Severe heart block without pacemaker, severe sinoatrial node dysfunction, known hypersensitivity to lidocaine or amide-type local anaesthetics
interactions: Additive cardiac depressant or arrhythmogenic effects with other antiarrhythmic agents; drugs that inhibit metabolism may increase systemic levels
monitoring: Continuous ECG monitoring during IV administration for arrhythmia management; observe for signs of local anaesthetic systemic toxicity (CNS excitation followed by depression, seizures) and cardiac toxicity
pregnancy: Use if necessary; regional or local anaesthetic use is generally acceptable in pregnancy but follow obstetric anaesthesia guidance
sideEffects: CNS effects (lightheadedness, tinnitus, tremor, seizures) at high or toxic levels; cardiovascular effects include bradycardia, hypotension and arrhythmias; allergic reactions are rare
clinicalPearls: Monitor plasma levels when using prolonged infusions or in patients with hepatic impairment; manage LAST with airway support and intravenous lipid emulsion therapy as per protocols
indication: Intravenous treatment of ventricular arrhythmias in emergency settings; local infiltration and topical analgesia per procedure-specific guidance
